title: Attribution Guard
eyebrow: Proposal, round 2 · no Claude credit in any of your 71 repos

short.lead: Your answers changed two things. Every repo you own is covered, forks included, and private repos too even though GitHub Free will not enforce a ruleset there. Merges stay as normal merge commits, so history is never rewritten and any failure stays visible. So the guarantee moves to our side: every place Claude credit can come from gets its own guard, and the house-rules hook refuses any merge until GitHub's check has passed. What exists today: the hook already refuses Claude credit in my commits and pull request text (hook.py, _ATTRIBUTION_TEXT_RES, eight patterns), but it does not check merges at all, and the claude.ai footer is added on claude.ai's servers where no hook reaches. The 2026-10-08 attribution plan named a shared GitHub check as an optional step that was never built.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what each part does and what it needs from you.
items: The hook keeps refusing Claude credit before anything is written

Unchanged: commits authored as Claude, Co-Authored-By lines, Claude-Session lines and Claude links in pull request or issue text are refused in every session, cloud or local. This is the first layer, and it is why the footer has been the only thing getting through.
A GitHub check reads every commit, the title, the description and comments

Runs on every pull request in all 71 repos, public and private, as pull_request_target so a pull request cannot edit the check to pass itself. It fails on any Claude author, committer or text pattern, using the same pattern file as the hook so the two cannot drift.
The hook refuses any merge until that check has passed

New in the hook: a merge through the GitHub tools, gh pr merge, or a git push to a default branch is refused unless the pull request's attribution check is green on its latest commit, and the merge message itself is checked too. This is what covers private repos on Free: every merge I or another session make goes through it.
Public repos also get GitHub's own block

On the 54 public repos, a ruleset makes the check required with nobody on the bypass list, so even a merge made outside a session is refused. GitHub Free cannot do this for the 17 private repos; the merge gate covers those.
The claude.ai footer is removed from descriptions and comments

The check also runs when a description or comment is posted or edited and removes the matching lines. This edits text, not history: GitHub keeps the edit record, so the footer's appearance stays on record.
Every push to a default branch is checked, and a failure opens an issue

If Claude credit ever reaches a default branch, by any route, the audit opens an issue in that repo naming the commit and the matching line, so a failure is recorded where you will see it, never hidden. Nothing is rewritten.
One script installs it on all 71 repos you own

tools/attribution_guard_install.py adds a short workflow file calling the shared check in AjsClaudeCodeTools, and the ruleset on public repos. It has a dry-run mode, skips repos owned by other people, and is safe to re-run for new repos. Adding the file to 71 default branches is the step that waits for your approval.
Approve the rollout after the test on focus-deck-app.

changes: The one copy of the check, cleanup and audit, called by every repo.
Only the in-session hook checks attribution, and only for what it sends.
Every pull request and default-branch push in all 71 repos is checked on GitHub itself.
The eight patterns move into one file (rules/attribution-patterns.json) that hook.py and the workflow both read.
Merge gate (changed: hook.py guard, hooks.json matcher)
Adds merges to what the hook checks.
Merges are not checked at all.
A merge is refused until the attribution check is green, and the merge message is checked.
Merges by a person in the GitHub website are not covered by the hook. On public repos the ruleset covers them; on private repos the audit records them.
Installs the caller workflow on all 71 repos and the ruleset on the 54 public ones.
One command covers every repo you own and can be re-run for new ones.
Your merge settings are left exactly as they are; no squash.
choices: On private repos, should merges through the GitHub website be stopped too?
You are the only person merging there by hand; the merge gate covers every agent merge, and the audit opens an issue if a hand merge ever carries Claude credit.
Pro ($4 a month) lets GitHub enforce the ruleset on private repos too, closing the last gap. Only worth it if hand merges on private repos happen often.
This is the one gap that cannot be closed from our side on Free: GitHub has no way for an outside tool to block its own merge button.
When the audit finds Claude credit on a default branch, what should happen?
Open an issue naming the commit
The failure stays in history and is recorded where you will see it.
Open an issue and also push a fix commit
A fix commit cannot remove text from an earlier commit, so it adds noise without removing the credit.

wrapup.summary: Layered guards on our side for all 71 repos: the hook refuses Claude credit and now also refuses any merge until GitHub's check passes, GitHub's ruleset adds its own block on public repos, and an audit records anything that ever gets through.
wrapup.changing: Two new files and a hook change in AjsClaudeCodeTools, then one small workflow file in each of the 71 repos and a ruleset on the 54 public ones. Merge settings and history are untouched.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the two choices.
wrapup.next: I build the check and the merge gate, prove them on focus-deck-app with a deliberately Claude-credited pull request, then show you the dry-run list before the rollout.
